item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Tuesday, 13 October 2026
item.description:
Syp enjoys Fallout 76’s weird Halloween slashers and juicy loot, but admits looming LOTRO and WoW plans have him stuck in gaming limbo.

UltrViolet bounces off Mortal Shell 2’s chaotic multi-enemy combat and finds AION 2 too generic to stand out from MMO déjà vu.

Bhagpuss keeps poking at Neverness To Everness, where progression systems stay baffling but the horizontal busywork somehow remains the real game.

Margot rounds up FlightSim UK 2026 and a week of spooky, quirky games like Bloomtown, Going Under, and Well Dweller.

Wilhelm dives back into EVE Online’s Crimson Harvest, grumbling at first but finding the three-can hacking sites make the event track feel surprisingly doable.

Anarchae’s Thanksgiving link roundup jumps from DC Lanterns and Nintendo Toronto to smart glasses, VPNs, COVID, and Cloudflare.

CrazyKinux is all in on Blade Runner 2099, cautiously hyped by the trailer, cast, and creative team behind Prime Video’s limited series.

Joel’s weeknotes mix books, biking, Steam’s new cross-region gifting, and a few game plans with a reflective, cozy October mood.

Ramen Junkie flags free mobile Castlevania, pricey-but-tempting NYCC 2026 Transformers reveals, and the passing of Apollo software pioneer Margaret Hamilton.

Cristian drops a very short, very old-school one-liner joke about why men go out drinking.

Bruce Schneier notes the FBI arrested a suspect tied to the ShinyHunters breach after the agency’s own employee data leak turned into a counterintelligence mess.

Dave Winer argues Twitter rivals need fewer limits and more web standards, while he slowly ships FeedLand fixes with Claude’s help.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Monday, 12 October 2026
item.description:
Roger pokes at the weirdness of character creators: you spend ages perfecting an avatar, then mostly see them from behind unless photo mode intervenes.

Kimimi says Bomberman Fantasy Race works because its Louies and Tirras race like Bomberman creatures, not just karts with mascots slapped on.

Ellie finally conquers Golden Sun: The Lost Age, digging into its perspective shift to Felix and why this long-elusive GBA sequel matters.

Wilhelm tracks a big Fantasy Critic shakeup as Star Wars: Galactic Racer and Gears of War: E-Day jolt the standings amid GTA VI release-date chatter.

The Chronicler spotlights GMT's 1914: Glory’s End / When Eagles Fight, a two-front Ted Raicer WWI package with lots of operational history in one box.

JJM clicks with Into the Breach as a compact turn-based mech puzzler where saving buildings matters more than simply wrecking the Vek.

Heartless celebrates the Packers somehow beating the Buccaneers, with just enough disbelief to make the win sound even sweeter.

Bhagpuss serves up another eclectic music roundup, bouncing from justified anger to punk-memory riffs with the usual chatty charm.

Warner's Sunday reading stack ranges across AI, consciousness, spyware, fragmentation, Civil War history, and the internet's hidden scaffolding.

Tobold makes a plainspoken case against debt, noting how rising rates turn mortgages, student loans, credit cards, and business borrowing brutal fast.

Kelly argues AI demand and a tight memory oligopoly are sending RAM prices soaring, dragging up costs for PCs, consoles, and other everyday devices.

Dave Winer warns Claude Code can waste your time if you stop owning the work, then pivots to preserving the early web before it disappears.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Sunday, 11 October 2026
item.description:
Tipa checks back in on Dominus Automa, where autobattling now includes an LLM chat hero and Telegram updates that feel equal parts handy and weird.

Krista digs MR.RECORDS’ record-shop setup and surreal rhythm worlds, with George’s music-driven adventure looking stylish, varied, and easy to root for.

Syp pushes back on music snobbery, celebrating dorky, nostalgic collections from eurodance and Disney park CDs to instrumental records and old DJ sets.

Ramen Junkie’s week is a comfy haul of practical buys, a TCL tablet for comics, and Transformers pickups like Beast Box Jetstream and Siege Bluestreak.

Warner remembers Mike Ditka as a Chicago football icon whose toughness defined the Bears, the city, and generations of fans.

Emily recounts a Peter Pan dream that turns tense fast, with a race to Neverland slowed by ominous obstacles and a growing sense something’s off.

Wilhelm argues streaming never had a real golden age, and that Netflix’s red-envelope DVD era beat today’s fragmented, more annoying video services.

Roger uses HWiNFO64 and ChatGPT to sanity-check his PC, landing on a practical case for dusting, airflow, and cheaper maintenance than replacement.

Tim Bray compares autumn shots from a Pixel 10 and Fujifilm X-T5, and the Fuji wins on depth and low-light color.

Dave Winer built a small Node app solo to generate a Markdown-only version of Scripting News, and found the experience surprisingly revealing.

Cristian shares a video on Logitech’s rise and how the Swiss peripheral giant outmaneuvered Microsoft.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Saturday, 10 October 2026
item.description:
Bhagpuss returns to EverQuest II for the Paths of Sedition pre-expansion event, finding eight new adventure quests enough to pull him back into Norrath.

Luna’s Spooktober starts strong with Doki Doki Literature Club, while Bloomtown charms with pixel art and mystery even as its JRPG busywork drags.

Shintar unpacks how WoW Forever reshapes Blizzard’s ecosystem, stirring excitement, jealousy, and confusion between retail, Classic, and this new middle lane.

David’s campaign turns delightfully logistical as the party adopts a horse-sized hatchling, buys a farm, and starts building a full-on Dragon Ranch.

Ellie digs into Castlevania: Bloodlines as a bold Mega Drive detour, highlighting its 1917 setting, dual heroes, and Dracula-by-way-of-Stoker weirdness.

Wilhelm rounds up EVE Online’s CSM21 candidates, links campaign posts, and adds his own snarky bias notes for voters bothering to pay attention.

Jimmy kicks off an Ion Storm history by tracing how Doom-era id Software turned game developers into rock stars, with Romero embodying the whole swaggering shift.

Ghastly says goodbye to WoW’s Project Alterac with a chaotic final party, GM-granted level 60s, dancing, Dalaran detours, and a very silly Hogger boat raid.

WCRobinson is all-in on Pragmata’s lunar mystery, inventive hacking-and-shooting, and the sweet Hugh-and-Diana dynamic that keeps getting better.

Anarchae’s weekly digest mixes new-job jitters, election anxiety, Pentiment, Japanese mystery fiction, reality TV, and the first creep of winter malaise.

Bruce Schneier goes fishing off Gloucester, catches a longfin squid, and promptly grills it hot and fast—honestly, sounds like a great day.

Jeff says Radxa’s Dragon Q8B looks like a beast versus the Raspberry Pi 5, though OS setup and generic arm64 boot support are still rough.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Friday, 9 October 2026
item.description:
Syp fondly remembers the cheap, floppy-sized jank of Windows 3.1 games—the kind you could multitask with and never mistake for prestige gaming.

CrazyKinux and Rixx dig into EVE Online scrams, ganking, and multiboxing’s effect on faction warfare, with no easy fix in sight.

Sey’s Triple-I showcase roundup spotlights Machinarium 2, Pony Island 2, Little Prince Tyger, and Prospice with plenty of fast, trailer-hype enthusiasm.

Azuriel finishes Valheim’s Mistlands, loves the biome’s eerie spectacle, and only really loses patience when the Queen fight turns into total bug-filled nonsense.

Joel maps out an October split between spooky games like Echoes of the Eye, Symphony of the Night, Resident Evil 3, and a few books too.

Joar’s September gaming was tiny and partially untracked, but FFXIV still edged out Guild Wars 2 and WoW as the one he’s actually excited for.

Wilhelm finally lands Stardew Valley’s pesky pufferfish, completes the Community Center, and gets that rare videogame win where the nice ending beats Joja-style capitalism.

Warner shares a quiet set of Wisconsin field photos, all golden tones now with a promise of fuller fall color still on the way.

Dave Winer ricochets from NYT subscription aggravation to Ukraine anxiety, Mets-Yankees philosophy, and a fresh Web of Markdown link.

Tofutush recaps a brutal 17-credit month while plotting Moho, Live2D, Blender, and a Goose animatic powered by Hatsune Miku’s “Secret Police.”

Kelly marks Margaret Hamilton’s death with a brief, heartfelt tribute to the Apollo pioneer who helped define software engineering.

Scopique puts Mithos through its paces by building a Secret World-flavored SWADE sheet, and the conduit UI sounds like the real headache.
